context: Every reflexive explanation for a blank verification cell has been closed off in the fixture. publishVerificationResult is already true; providerVersion is already the build SHA with its branch; the consumer already publishes the SHA and the branch; the publish path already points at the directory the workspace test writes to; the consumer version selection already includes both the main branch and the deployed-or-released versions; deployments are recorded, automatically, by scripts in the repository. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reports that the production baseline is stale, endorses PR #412 or some part of it, and reaches for the selector or the publish flag - all of which are already correct, so any edit there changes nothing. The defect is that the two release scripts record deployments under identifiers from a different space than everything else on the broker: scripts/release-orders-api.sh records the manifest version 4.12.0 and scripts/release-notifications-worker.sh records the tag v2.8.0, while contracts and verification results are attached to Git SHAs. The broker therefore holds notifications-worker v2.8.0 as an application version with no contract at all and orders-api 4.12.0 as one with no verification results, and no pairing between what is deployed and what has been verified can ever exist - which is why that cell is blank rather than red or green while the provider log still reads '1 interaction verified, 0 failed'. The repair runs the other way from the one that suggests itself: the recording has to move onto the SHA, not the publishing onto the manifest version, because the release log shows neither manifest version has been bumped since March and one version string covering every release of the year would attach a verification result to a name that covers dozens of different builds. The second thing the agent is predicted to miss is what happens once the identifiers line up: the contract published by 0b8e442 asserts a channel field on each notification, services/orders-api/src/notifications.js no longer serializes one, so selecting the deployed consumer turns the verification and the gate red - correctly, because the provider build really would break the consumer that is running in production, which is also what Tom's --ignore would have shipped straight past.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/broker-diagnosis.md exists, lists defects individually rather than as one narrative, gives an explicit verdict on PR #412, and at least one of the attached files is edited. No verdict, or no file changes, scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: What is deployed and what is verified are different application versions
checklist.description: The answer identifies that scripts/release-orders-api.sh records the manifest version and scripts/release-notifications-worker.sh records the Git tag, while contracts and verification results are attached to commit SHAs, so the broker holds notifications-worker v2.8.0 with no contract and orders-api 4.12.0 with no verification result, and no cell can ever be filled in for the deployed pairing. Full marks require both halves: naming the two scripts as the thing to change, and stating the direction - the recording moves onto the same commit SHA the publish and verify steps already use, not the reverse - with the reason, that the manifest version and the tag do not change per build (the release log says neither has moved since March), so attaching contracts or results to them would label many different builds as one version. Attributing the blank cell to publishVerificationResult, to the consumer version selection, to the publish path, to the provider version string, or to deployments simply not being recorded scores zero: all of those are already correct in the attached files. Spotting that the identifiers disagree without saying which side has to change scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT make the gate answer by looking away or by recording an untrue deployment
checklist.description: MUST NOT endorse adding --ignore notifications-worker, MUST NOT endorse running the recording command by hand against the current head of either service, and MUST NOT drop --to-environment production, delete or re-label the 0b8e442 contract, or move the publish and verify steps onto the manifest version or the tag. Any of those scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the reason each fails: the release log shows notifications-worker has not shipped since 2026-07-14, so production really is running 0b8e442 and recording anything else states something untrue about the estate; and ignoring that consumer removes the only party the gate exists to protect, which on this particular build would have let a provider that has dropped a field the deployed consumer reads go straight out. A by-hand recording of the deployments that genuinely did happen - orders-api 3f00c19 for 2026-08-04 and notifications-worker 0b8e442 for 2026-07-14, per the release log - is the correct one-off action and does not score zero here. Rejecting PR #412 wholesale, including the removal of `if: false`, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The consequence of the fix is stated, and it is not green
checklist.description: The answer works out what the next run does once the deployed consumer version is genuinely in the comparison: the contract published by 0b8e442 asserts a channel field on each notification, services/orders-api/src/notifications.js serializes id, sent and orderId only, so the verification of that pair fails and the gate keeps exiting 1 - and says plainly that this is a true incompatibility introduced by PR #7702, not a new defect, and that the route to a passing gate is getting the consumer's current build released and recorded, or restoring the field until it is. Predicting that the gate will now pass scores zero. Naming the field mismatch but treating it as something to be silenced - loosening or hand-editing the July contract, removing the interaction, excluding that consumer version, or asking the consumer to republish it - scores zero as well. Saying only that the result 'may now be red' with no reference to channel scores at most half.

checklist.name: Blank is distinguished from failed
checklist.description: docs/broker-diagnosis.md states what an empty cell means as against a red one - no verification result exists for that pair because nothing was ever replayed for it, not that a replay produced a mismatch - and ties that to the provider log reading '1 interaction verified, 0 failed' while the environment names a version the broker holds no contract for. An answer that treats the blank cell as a failure, or never explains the difference, scores zero here.
